question: is the per-frame drift global gain, pixel noise, or a spatial change in the scene?
correction: TWO CORRECTIONS NOW, and the second is the bigger one. (1) An earlier report said per-frame gain normalisation cut drift from 43.3 to 0.81 counts. It did not: it compared raw counts against relative units. 43.686/111.18 = 0.393 and 43.226/109.71 = 0.394, so the reduction was 1.00x, not ~50x. That error is why gain_invariance.py could not work. (2) The 43.3 counts of drift were never drift at all. The captures on disk carry 19,200 bytes per frame, not the W*H*3//2 = 23,040 this file used to assume, so all but every sixth frame was torn -- rows 0..71 from frame k, rows 72..95 from frame k+1. The splice lands across row 72, which manufactures a horizontal band in every mis-read frame. The 'mains-derived LED flicker' banding this file measured, and the row-band-removal pass built on it, were the tear.
notes: THE BANDING WAS THE TORN FRAME. The previous run measured a row-dominant residual in the occupied capture (row-profile std 31.31 counts against col-profile std 7.08, column energy share 4.9%) and read that as mains-derived LED flicker. It is the row-72 splice of a mis-strided read: a horizontal step is flat across every column by construction. At the correct stride the profile INVERTS -- the occupied capture is now column-dominant (row-profile std 0.22 against col-profile std 0.30, column energy share 65%), which is the signature of a room feature rather than a horizontal band. The top-3 row-FFT energy share falls from 44% to 12%, so there is no dominant band left to attribute to a lamp.

THE EMPTY ROOM'S DRIFT IS AT THE NOISE FLOOR, and its gain fraction is meaningless. The empty capture's adjacent |diff| is 0.006 counts -- far below the 8-bit quantisation of the sensor -- and its residual 2x2 averaging ratio is 0.511, which is the ~0.50 of independent per-pixel noise. 'Gain explains -14.0%' is a division artefact at that magnitude, not a physical claim, and the MIXED classification is the pre-registered rule's honest fallback rather than a finding.

The verdict reports the capture where gain explains the MOST of the drift. That selection rule is the pre-existing one and is unchanged; with the new numbers it selects OCCUPIED (2.6%) rather than EMPTY (-14.0%).
method: least-squares fit of one scalar k per adjacent frame pair through the origin; residual is what a global gain cannot explain. Noise test: RMS of the residual after 2x2 block averaging, relative to before -- pure independent noise gives ~0.50, structure survives.

supersedes.why: Re-measured on 2026-10-20. The previous run read both captures at W*H*3//2 = 23,040 bytes per frame; the captures on disk carry 19,200 bytes per frame, so all but every sixth frame was torn (rows 0..71 from frame k, rows 72..95 from frame k+1). The previous numbers are recorded here rather than silently overwritten.

supersedes.verdict_changed: The verdict text is expected to change, and the reason is not a new measurement: the thing the previous verdict classified was the torn frame. A horizontal splice across row 72 produces exactly the flat column profile and the strong low row-frequency content that the previous run read as mains-derived LED flicker. Whether the new numbers still support a banding claim is stated by the new verdict and must be read on its own.

verdict: Gain explains 2.6% of the drift in OCCUPIED (facing, speaking), and the residual noise ratio is 0.69. MIXED: gain explains 2.6%, averaging ratio 0.69
